question: Why can a single dose of HPV vaccine give protection that most protein vaccines need several doses for?
answer: Because of its shape. Its protein, L1, assembles itself into empty virus shells, each carrying 360 copies in a tight, repeating lattice. That pattern cross-links the receptors on antibody-making B cells and recruits long-lived ones. In 2022 the WHO endorsed one-dose schedules; a Kenyan trial had found about 97% efficacy 18 months after one dose.
move: How a signal is arranged can matter as much as how strong it is.
reference: Schiller & Lowy, Explanations for the high potency of HPV prophylactic vaccines, Vaccine, 2018
